Generate data from a model's priors (deprecated)

Source: R/ctGenerate.R
ctGenerateFromPriors.Rd

Deprecated. Use ctGenerate(fromPriors = TRUE), which does the same. ctStanGenerate is an alias and is also deprecated.

Usage

ctGenerateFromPriors(
  cts,
  datastruct = NA,
  is = FALSE,
  fullposterior = TRUE,
  nsamples = 200,
  parsonly = FALSE,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L),
  backend = c("auto", "julia", "stan"),
  n.subjects = 20,
  Tpoints = NULL,
  dtmean = 1
)

Arguments

cts

A model from ctModel or ctModelConvertOMX, or a fit from either backend, which supplies its model and design.

datastruct

Long format data structure as used by ctsem, giving the subjects, times and missing observations to generate. Ignored when cts is a fit, which uses its own data. If NA and cts is a model, a balanced design of n.subjects subjects observed at Tpoints occasions dtmean apart is used.

is

Deprecated and ignored, with a warning if set.

fullposterior

Generate from the full prior, or from its mode (the raw origin)?

nsamples

How many samples to generate?

parsonly

If TRUE, only return samples of raw parameters, don't generate data.

cores

Number of cpu cores to use.

backend

Which engine generates data from each parameter draw: 'auto' (the default) uses 'julia' when a julia session is available and 'stan' otherwise, or 'julia' or 'stan'. The parameter draws come from the model's prior and are the same either way. Not used with parsonly=TRUE.

n.subjects, Tpoints, dtmean

The design used when cts is a model and no datastruct is given. Tpoints defaults to the model's own when it has one. The default n.subjects is smaller than ctGenerate's because nsamples datasets are returned.

Value

List containing Y, an array of nsamples by data rows by manifest variables, and llrow, an array of nsamples by data rows log likelihoods. With parsonly=TRUE, the prepared model with the prior draws in $stanfit$rawposterior and $stanfit$transformedpars.

Examples

# \donttest{
#generate and plot samples from prior predictive
priorpred <- ctGenerateFromPriors(cts = ctstantestfit,cores=2,nsamples = 50)
# backend = 'auto' generates with julia where it is available. Julia keeps
# running between calls, holding what it has compiled; this ends it.
if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) ctJuliaKill("session")
# }
